details:
Ok so to put it simply. The HTC Vive controllers have touch activation, and emotes can be activated just by swiping your thumb or touching the general side being there are 8 total sections on both controllers that can be activated with touch sense. 8 pieces meaning 8 emotes, and 16 total on both controllers. Take a model with multiple emotes which require loading specific scripts like dances, songs etc. now throw 10 people into a room with the same setup and having them move/look around. Now in my belief having touch sense on the Vive controllers activate these emote pieces even though you are not attempting to use the emote but the game performs a draw call anyways causing your game to stutter.
As I have a model of my own which I use just going around worlds and I notice every time I go to walk backwards it activates my dance emote for a split second and then vanishes. This causes a draw call on my end. Then because the emote was loaded under a draw call, pressing any other emote slot will re-activate the last emote being the dance emote and cause 2 draw calls to happen because it has to load the previous emote, deactivate it and reactivate the other one (at least I think). 
I have an emote with some particles being hearts and if I move in the direction that activates the emote, the emote activates under a draw call and then is placed under the pre-load and deactivates, but if I press per say open hand it reactivates said emote again and deactivates it. Causing more draw calls if there was an emote on my open hand, then it would cause 2 or more draw calls to happen.

I'm not sure if this is client sided or if it is global. I would think this would be the cause to stuttering worlds and the reason why your game may take forever to load. Because it is being forced to do draw calls when ever emotes are being activated. 
If emotes were pre-loaded under the model then activating the emotes would be seamless, this would only make the model a larger size in file but also it would take a bit longer to load depending on the user's internet speed.

Another fix could possibly be changing how emotes are activated, instead of pressing on the side where the emote activates, you have to swipe to get the emote. I'm not sure if this is already a thing, however I can just tap one side/angle and it activates an emote. 
Either that or change how emotes are activated to activate draw calls. Maybe have them take a little longer time for activation to prevent draw calls on both sides? maybe moving it from the .2ms to .4ms or longer. 
I understand it would change the pace at which emotes can be used, but I believe it would give better performance while using the draw call system.

Let's see what other users have to say about this.
title: HTC Vive controllers w/ emotes cause draw calls?
